ogDesc: 10 places that Lopburi locals actually eat at — old Thai Phuan recipes, duck noodles, chicken rice, freshwater fish by the river, and a fresh-milk cafe. With signature dishes and prices.
eyebrow: Eat Like the Locals in Lopburi · Updated 2026
intro: Lopburi is a city where eating well doesn't require following any trend. From old Thai Phuan recipes in the historic quarter, to famous duck noodles over in Tha Wung, to a cafe sitting quietly in a garden — we've curated 10 places that locals genuinely eat at and that travelers talk about. There's something for a full meal, a light bite, or an evening sweet.
chips: 🍜 Duck noodles and tom yam noodles

blocks.html:
The charm of Lopburi is a small city that's easy and pleasant to eat your way through. The old-town area around San Phra Kan and Wat Choeng Tha is lined with heritage restaurants, and the Thai Phuan flavors here are handmade in a way that's hard to find anywhere else. The riverside side of the city has floating-raft restaurants where you can eat freshwater fish with a cool breeze. Come evening, the city shifts into fresh-milk cafes and garden settings. A province where you can eat from morning to late at night without getting in a car.

This list has both long-standing institutions and places a younger crowd makes a point of photographing. Mat Mi Thai Phuan is a decades-old restaurant famous for its nam prik and gaeng kua hed phao. Krua Mai Hom takes hard-to-find royal Thai dishes like gaeng ranjuan and chu chi jakkraphat and serves them in a modern setting. Kuayteow Ped Phuuyai Prachum in Tha Wung is a bowl that road-trippers on that route always stop for. Dom Khao Man Gai has been at the top of the local list for years. Pick two or three places in one trip and you'll get the real taste of Lopburi.

blocks.name: Mat Mi Thai Phuan
blocks.signature: Homemade fresh-pounded pla ra, gaeng ranjuan, phad phed pla duk, old-style Thai Phuan dishes
blocks.descHtml:
If you come to Lopburi and want local food you genuinely can't find in other cities, Mat Mi Thai Phuan is the restaurant that locals and reviewers alike mention in almost one voice. The place has been part of the city for over 30 years. The owner, Pa Tim (Nawarat), is a Ban Mi native of Thai Phuan heritage, and her old Phuan recipes — light on coconut milk, heavy on pla ra (fermented fish) and aromatics — produce a home-style food that is simultaneously bold and balanced. The right choice for anyone who wants genuinely local food rather than a standard Thai menu.

The dish reviewers most say you can't miss is the homemade fresh-pounded pla ra: fermented pla kradie (crucian carp) from Ban Mi, wrapped in banana leaf, charcoal-roasted, then pounded with galangal, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaf, shallots, and krachai. Eat it with fresh vegetables — the herb fragrance is remarkable. Another signature is gaeng kua hed phao pla krai, and the gaeng ranjuan is a rare ancient Thai soup with a thick, aromatic broth that you can barely describe. For bold flavors try phad phed pla duk, or the kai khem phad prik khing pla duk fu (salted-egg stir-fried crispy catfish). For the adventurous, there's kai jiao kai mod daeng (red-ant egg omelette) and pla som fak thong. Most reviews agree: richly flavored, nearly every dish delivering on the original recipe.

The setting is an old Thai house, warm, like having a meal at a relative's home. There are khanom thuai snacks to nibble while you wait. Most dishes are 100–150 THB, averaging around 251–500 THB per person if you order several. Located on Phra Sri Mahosat Road, between the Phra Narai roundabout and the Sra Kaew roundabout — a small side street that needs a moment's attention to spot, but there's parking and they take credit cards.

Open daily around 10:00–20:30, usually closed on the 15th of each month — call ahead if you're visiting around that date. This place is popular because it's one of the very few restaurants that still maintains a complete Thai Phuan recipe base, using ingredients Pa Tim grows herself or sources from trusted suppliers. For anyone on a heritage food trail, or wanting to feed older family members a genuinely traditional meal, this is the right place.
mustOrder: Gaeng kua hed phao pla krai
blocks.bestFor: First meal in Lopburi, authentic local food with family
blocks.hours: 10:00–20:30 daily (closed on the 15th of each month)

blocks.name: Kuayteow Ped Phuuyai Prachum
blocks.signature: Duck noodles in rich broth, sweet tender duck meat, plenty of toppings
blocks.descHtml:
If you're driving through Tha Wung and hungry, this is the stop that Lopburi locals nod toward without hesitation. Kuayteow Ped Phuuyai Prachum is an old roadside restaurant on Highway 311, Bang Khu Sub-district, open for over 45 years. It began as a pork noodle shop passed down from the owner's parents, before Phuuyai Prachum switched to duck and turned it into the neighborhood's signature dish. Ideal for anyone looking for a simple, satisfying midday meal on the road between Lopburi's sights, or for noodle hunters tracking down a famous duck bowl.

The must-order is the duck noodles in soup — available in both thin rice noodles and yellow egg noodles; many regulars especially like the egg noodles. The star is the amber broth: clear but concentrated, built from phalo spices and palm sugar toasted until lightly fragrant, then simmered low and long. The duck is carefully sourced, sweet, tender, and bouncy — not tough or gamey. Reviewers consistently single out the fresh-daily fried garlic and pork cracklings that are scattered on top, fragrant enough to finish without adding condiments. For more duck, order the chopped duck meat on the side — it's worth it.

Pricing is very friendly: noodles at 40 THB a bowl, chopped duck at 70 THB a plate. The setting is a simple local shophouse — quick and easy. Open daily in the morning through early afternoon, around 08:30–15:30 (some days from 09:00). Midday gets busy because this place has appeared in several food programs. Come a bit early and the full menu is yours with no queue.
blocks.bestFor: Lunch on the road while touring Lopburi

blocks.name: Kuayteow Luan Lopburi (Sra Kaew Roundabout)
blocks.cuisine: Beef and pork noodles, clear broth
blocks.signature: Clear beef or pork noodles, homemade tendon meatballs, piping hot broth
blocks.descHtml:
If you've just stepped off the bus at Lopburi bus terminal and need something that tastes authentically local, the noodle shop Luan at the corner of the Sra Kaew roundabout is the first name many Lopburi people think of. This shop has been open across multiple generations and become a name the city knows well — a clear-broth noodle shop with both beef and pork options, good for a solo visitor, a family, or anyone passing through, since the shophouse is spacious with two full shop units, street parking in front.

The regular order is clear beef noodles — you can mix sliced beef and stewed beef in the same bowl. The stewed beef is braised until meltingly tender; the sliced beef is lightly marinated with a gentle sweetness, as reviewers consistently note. The real hero is the clear broth: fragrant, rounded, clean — people say you can drink it straight without adding a single condiment. The other item not to overlook is the homemade tendon meatball — firm, fresh-tasting, so good that the shop also sells them wholesale. Beef fans should try the mixed beef offal noodles alongside rice, or if you prefer no beef, there's marinated pork noodles too.

Pricing is very easy: noodles start at 45 THB, the offal bowl and specials run 60–90 THB, average spend per person well under a hundred baht. Location is convenient — right at the Sra Kaew roundabout in the city center, near the bus terminal. Coming from Big C, use exit 2 and you'll see the shop at the corner. Open morning through evening daily.

One thing to know: the shop operates separate day and night sittings, so if you're planning a late-night visit, call ahead to confirm. Most of the menu is in Thai, so foreign visitors may need to point at a picture or ask staff for help — worth doing, because this kind of clear-broth noodle shop built up over generations is hard to replicate.
mustOrder: Clear beef noodles — sliced and stewed beef
blocks.bestFor: First meal in the province, arriving at the bus terminal
blocks.spice: Season to your own taste, not spicy by default

blocks.name: Dom Khao Man Gai
blocks.signature: Chicken rice with tender meat, shiitake mushroom broth reminiscent of Chinese herbal soup, house fermented-soybean dipping sauce
blocks.descHtml:
Ask any Lopburi local which chicken rice shop to try and Dom Khao Man Gai comes up almost every time. The shop has been part of the city for years — formerly on Phahon Yothin Road across from Lotus before relocating to the Z-ONE Market (Sat-1 Market) area where parking is much easier. A great stop for anyone passing through who wants a straightforward, satisfying meal, or for families who want reliable, honest chicken rice.

The dish everyone orders is the chicken rice — available as steamed or fried chicken. What reviewers consistently single out: the chicken is cut into generous pieces, the plate piled almost to overflow, and the meat is soft without being dry. Some plates come with a bonus of congealed chicken blood. But the true hero is the broth — shiitake mushrooms are added to the stock, giving it a fragrant black pepper note that evokes a Chinese herbal soup. Warm and satisfying to drink. The other thing not to overlook is the house fermented-soybean dipping sauce: a sharp, spicy-sweet heat with ginger that can be topped up freely. For bold-spice lovers, this sauce makes the meal. Beyond chicken rice, there's also satay pork and charcoal-braised pork trotter to add on.

Pricing is easy on the wallet: most items under a hundred baht, genuinely good value. The space is wide, clean, well-staffed so service moves fast even during busy periods. The shop has appeared on food programs, spreading the name Dom Khao Man Gai well beyond the province.

Open morning through afternoon, roughly 07:30–16:00 (Sundays may run later). Come in the late morning through noon — popular items can sell out, and even though the shop has moved, the regulars followed. A good sign that the flavors haven't changed.
blocks.bestFor: First meal in the province / passing through and want good value
blocks.spice: Adjustable via fermented-soybean sauce and ginger
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: chicken rice · Pauloleong2002 / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 4.0)

blocks.name: Krua Mai Hom
blocks.signature: Gaeng ranjuan with old-recipe nam prik, chu chi jakkraphat, grilled pork with jaew dip, ancient royal Thai dishes
blocks.descHtml:
Krua Mai Hom is an ancient Thai royal-style restaurant in the city of Lopburi that takes rare, hard-to-find heritage recipes and presents them in a way that a modern diner can access. The building is a two-unit commercial shophouse, decorated in a modern-loft gray-black tone — cool and sharp, air-conditioned and comfortable, seating around 50–60. Good for a special family meal, a couple looking for a comfortable table, or anyone who wants to try Thai food that almost no other restaurant makes anymore.

The dish people mention most is the nam prik mai hom — made from roasted chili pounded with roasted fish, then ground with a house spice mix; the flavor opens sour before settling into a gentle sweetness. Eat it with fresh vegetables. The next essential is gaeng ranjuan: the restaurant makes it with fragrant grilled pork, sauced with nam prik pounded overnight, and the flavor — sour, salty, spicy, sweet — is layered in a way that's hard to put into words. The chu chi jakkraphat is a Thai-Chinese fusion: minced pork mixed with prawns, steamed then fried, served alongside snapper, topped with chu chi sauce and kaffir lime leaf. And the grilled pork with jaew dip is a table that many tables order again. Most reviews note rich, bold flavors, coconut milk that isn't heavy, fast service, attentive staff, and convenient parking.

Dish prices around 60–160 THB; per-person average 101–500 THB — good value for the skill. Located on Phra Piya Road; from the Phra Narai roundabout head toward the prison, right side before Ramkhamhaeng University Lopburi. Open 10:00–20:00, closed on the 1st and 16th of every month.

This place draws regulars because genuinely serious ancient Thai food is rare in Lopburi, and the plating photographs well. Google rating 4.5 from hundreds of reviews confirms it. On weekends it fills up; some royal-style dishes are made fresh to order so allow a few minutes. And always check the closing dates — the 1st and 16th — before you head out.
blocks.bestFor: Special family meal, wanting to try ancient royal Thai cuisine
blocks.hours: 10:00–20:00 daily (closed on the 1st and 16th of each month)

blocks.name: Pae Baan Rimnam Lopburi
blocks.signature: River fish dishes, herb-steamed clams, forest curry, fried fish cakes, riverside raft atmosphere
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Lopburi and want a restaurant for a long, relaxed meal with fresh river fish and a cool riverside view, Pae Baan Rimnam is the place that people near San Phra Kan and Wat Choeng Tha bring up regularly. It's a garden-raft restaurant extending over the Lopburi river — an old wooden structure, expanded over the years but still carrying its original character. Sitting in the natural breeze, watching boats and the current drift by — the right place for anyone who wants to escape the noise and eat without rushing.

The regular orders are large freshwater fish — pla chon baan phae (snakehead), tom saeb pla kang (spicy catfish soup), lab pla raet, and pla kapong maeo mong (barramundi-style fish), which many regulars say is outstanding. For something to dip and share, there are herb-steamed clams with lemongrass and kaffir lime leaf fragrance. Forest curry and fried fish cakes go well as supporting dishes. Add lab moo thod, fried salt chicken, gaeng kua hoi khom, and shrimp marinated in fish sauce for a complete table. Most reviews praise the flavor, the freshness of the fish, and — a consistent point — the portion sizes, which are large enough that groups get excellent value.

Pricing around 251–500 THB per person if you're sharing a whole fish. Located in Soi Wat Choeng Tha, Phetrachat Road, near the old town — best reached by private car as the restaurant sits deep in a small lane. There's parking in front. Open daily around 10:00–22:00. Foreign visitors stopping in Lopburi also come here because a riverside setting like this is rare to find in the city center.

The restaurant is open-air, so midday is warm and the late-afternoon breeze is more pleasant. If coming as a group, call ahead to book a riverside table. Allow a few minutes to find the entrance lane. Once you're there, the atmosphere makes it worthwhile.
blocks.bestFor: Evening riverside dinner with friends or family
blocks.zone: Old Town (Wat Choeng Tha – San Phra Kan)
blocks.spice: Bold spice options (tom saeb, lab), adjustable

blocks.name: Chalerm Thai Kuayteow Tom Yam
blocks.signature: Tom yam noodles with large river prawns, pork tom yam, bold sour-spicy broth
blocks.descHtml:
If you're in Lopburi and want tom yam noodles done properly, Chalerm Thai Kuayteow Tom Yam is the restaurant that both locals and visitors talk about regularly. Located in the Phrommasat Sub-district, near Wat Phrommasat, about 700 metres from the old-town historic core. The shop has been making bold tom yam noodles for years and has been certified by the Lopburi Chamber of Commerce as a provincial specialty, consecutively. For anyone who loves sour-forward, spicy-following, packed bowls — this is the place.

The bowl most people order is the mixed seafood tom yam — large prawns, squid, fish, and soft-boiled egg all together. The broth opens sour-sweet, spice sits at a pleasant medium level. For meat lovers, the large river prawn tom yam or the pork and lime tom yam both hit the same theme. The broth is intense and well-seasoned throughout. A popular side snack is the fried pork wonton (about 50 THB) — crispy and good alongside the noodles. And there's red pork rice for anyone who'd rather skip the noodles.

Another draw is the retro interior: the restaurant is decorated with collected old objects — vintage TVs, antique telephones, artifacts from another era — everywhere you look. There's both air-conditioned and open sections, comfortable for families or groups. A small touch: there are lucky numbers under each bowl to read after you've eaten. Pricing per person in the range of 101–250 THB depending on what you order — fair value for the portions.

The restaurant opens midday around 08:00–16:00, closed Mondays. Parking both in front and behind. Easy to stop at while visiting temples or the old town. Since it's a lunch-only spot, anyone planning an evening visit will miss it — come in the late morning for fresh ingredients and no wait. A solid first-stop pin for Lopburi.
mustOrder: Pork and lime tom yam noodles
blocks.bestFor: Lunch for bold tom yam lovers, families and groups

blocks.name: Chef Un Steak
blocks.area: Mueang Lopburi District (Bridge 33) and Phatthana Nikhom District (Soi 12), Lopburi
blocks.signature: Australian sirloin and tenderloin steak, black pepper pork steak, oven-braised pork ribs in sauce
blocks.descHtml:
When it comes to steak in Lopburi that has become a genuine word-of-mouth name, Chef Un is the place. The chef trained and cooked abroad for several years — in Canada and the United States — before returning to open a small restaurant called Baan Suan Grill Place at Soi 12, Phatthana Nikhom District, starting in 1999, which became the original. A second branch later opened in the city center near Bridge 33 (below Lopburi Residence Hotel). The distinguishing quality: carefully sourced meat — S-Pure pork, Australian beef — marinated in the chef's own sauce before going on the grill. A great choice for families, groups of friends, or couples who want a properly skilled steak without the hotel price tag.

The dishes ordered most are the large Australian sirloin steak, tenderloin steak with mushroom sauce, black pepper pork steak (tender and aromatic), and oven-braised pork ribs in tomato sauce simmered until falling off the bone. Other popular choices include beef grilled with jaew dip, basil beef with fried egg, and salmon steak. Every steak plate comes with garlic bread and salad. Most reviews note that the meat is tender, the salmon is fragrant and sweet from the grill, and the barbecue sauce paired with the jaew dip cuts through any richness well. Many say the quality exceeds the price by a comfortable margin.

Pricing per person roughly 100–250 THB for a single plate or pork steak; imported beef dishes push higher. The space is small, air-conditioned, plainly decorated — the focus is on the food. Bridge 33 branch open daily 11:00–21:00. The original Soi 12 Phatthana Nikhom branch open 11:00–19:30 (closed on the 1st and 16th of each month). At peak times seats fill quickly due to the small size — calling ahead to reserve is worth it. A must-stop if you're passing through Lopburi and want a genuinely well-made steak.
mustOrder: Oven-braised pork ribs in tomato sauce
blocks.bestFor: Chef-quality steak meal with family or friends
blocks.hours: Bridge 33: 11:00–21:00 daily · Soi 12 Phatthana Nikhom: 11:00–19:30 (closed on the 1st and 16th of each month)
blocks.spice: Jaew dip and basil dishes are spicy, adjustable

blocks.name: Nom Buri
blocks.signature: Cold fresh milk, Nom Buri blended, ovaltine cold sandwich, toast, relaxed evening atmosphere
blocks.descHtml:
If it's a Lopburi evening and you're not ready to head back, Nom Buri is the fresh-milk shop that locals like to meet at. Located on Ramdecho Road in the Route 2 area, next to Scala shop. It's a cute fresh-milk cafe that opens from the evening through late night — good for sitting after dinner, coming as a couple, a group of friends, or with family, since the shop divides into several zones: a cool air-conditioned room, an outdoor section on artificial grass, and a second-floor open-air terrace. Soft background music throughout. The atmosphere hits just right.

The most frequently ordered items are cold fresh milk and the Nom Buri blended, the house signature. For those who like soft and sweet, the ovaltine cold sandwich and the taro cold sandwich are hits. Toast fans have butter-milk toast and honey toast to choose from. Beyond desserts there's also a savory option — fresh prawn salad — for something to line the stomach. Most reviews say the milk is fragrant and delicious, nearly every bread item is good, the shop is nicely decorated and photographable, and it's cited by many as the fresh-milk spot to try when visiting Lopburi.

Pricing is very approachable: drinks start around 39–49 THB, cold sandwiches around 69 THB, toast around 45 THB, prawn salad around 89 THB. Most items well under a hundred baht. Two people can sit comfortably without spending much. The shop opens in the evenings through late at night.

One thing to note: the shop is on the street with no private parking lot — you'll need to park along the road nearby. Some nights it's busy and music from neighboring shops can be audible. But if you want a corner to sit with cold milk, warm toast, and a long conversation in Lopburi at night, Nom Buri is the right call.
blocks.bestFor: Evening to late night sit with friends
blocks.libCredit: Illustrative image: dessert · Ilya Plekhanov / Wikimedia (CC BY-SA 3.0)

blocks.name: About Coffee Garden
blocks.signature: Fresh coffee, cakes and baked goods, single-dish meals, relaxed outdoor garden setting
blocks.descHtml:
If you're a coffee drinker passing through Lopburi, About Coffee Garden is one of the shops that locals around here mention most. A small coffee shop at the intersection of Soi Chaloem Phra Kiat, started by an owner who is a genuine barista. The charm of this place is fresh-roasted coffee — quality beans, intensely aromatic, with many reviewers calling it genuinely excellent. The shop's standout is the AB Coffee — a blend that was used in the National Thailand Barista Championship in 2015. The technique and flavor are credentialed.

The most ordered items are the iced Americano (around 60–80 THB) — full-bodied, cleanly acidic with a berry note — and Dirty Coffee (75 THB), where the coffee oil cuts against creamy milk in a well-balanced way. For something fragrant and different, try the orange Americano using medium-roast beans — bright, faintly sweet. And the 50% dark espresso is intense and fragrant without going bitter. Beyond coffee there are cakes, baked goods like almond croissants (59 THB), and single-dish meals: chicken salad, basil fried rice, and other light plates. Most items start in the low hundreds; coffee from around 55 THB.

The space splits into two zones: a cool air-conditioned room and an outdoor garden with camp-style furniture on a gravel floor, surrounded by green plants — genuinely relaxing. The building is painted black with an AB about coffee garden sign — easy to spot. Good for a quiet coffee sit, a work meeting, or buying fresh-roasted beans to take home. Parking available, free wifi, accepts credit cards, and does delivery.

Closed on Wednesdays; other days open around 07:00–16:00. Morning weekends can be busy since the shop is not large. Allow a few extra minutes if you're coming as a group. Google rating 4.5 from several hundred reviews — most citing coffee quality as the top reason to come — and staff that are genuinely friendly. A coffee drinker's stop in Lopburi worth not missing.
blocks.bestFor: Coffee lovers, morning and mid-morning garden chill

blocks.title: Know Before You Eat in Lopburi

items.title: Getting Around
items.text: Grab works in the city center but coverage is thinner than Bangkok. The old-town area around San Phra Kan is walkable to several restaurants. For spots outside the city — like the duck noodles in Tha Wung or Chef Un Steak's Phatthana Nikhom branch — a private car or rental is more convenient.

items.title: Paying
items.text: Street stalls and single-dish restaurants mostly work on cash. Some accept PromptPay (QR transfer). Sit-down restaurants and cafes sometimes accept PromptPay but credit cards are not yet widespread at smaller shops.

items.title: Avoiding Queues
items.text: Popular places get busy at midday and on weekends. Come before noon or on a weekday for a comfortable seat. Some chicken rice and noodle spots sell out in the afternoon — arriving in the morning through midday is safer.

items.title: Language and Menus
items.text: Most local restaurants have Thai-only menus. Staff generally speak basic English. Pointing at pictures or using Google Translate works well. Some cafes and ancient Thai restaurants have illustrated menus that make ordering easier.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: No tip expected at street stalls and single-dish restaurants. At sit-down venues with table service, rounding up or leaving a small amount of change is a polite gesture. No fixed rule.

items.title: Old-Town Wildlife
items.text: The old-town area around San Phra Kan has a significant monkey population. Don't carry food or bags of food openly, and keep an eye on glasses, phones, and valuables. Eating inside a closed restaurant is the most comfortable option.

blocks.title: Plan 1–2 Days of Eating in Lopburi
blocks.html:
Lopburi is fun to eat through all day if you sequence it well. Start breakfast at Dom Khao Man Gai — famous for its shiitake mushroom broth and house fermented-soybean sauce. Or swing by Kuayteow Ped Phuuyai Prachum in Bang Khu if you're driving through Tha Wung. Lunch can stay in the old town: Mat Mi Thai Phuan and Krua Mai Hom are both in the city, both suited for a serious, bold Thai meal.

In the late afternoon, switch scenes to Pae Baan Rimnam near Wat Choeng Tha — order river fish with herb-steamed clams and sit with a riverside breeze. Then close the evening at Nom Buri, which opens at night, or About Coffee Garden if you want a garden cafe. Popular places fill up on weekends; arriving before noon or on a weekday makes everything smoother.

blocks.text: For multiple meals across Lopburi's old town and riverside, staying one night in the city center means you eat without rushing — morning chicken rice, evening riverside dinner. Book a well-located stay first and let the meals follow.

faq.q: Which restaurant is the most famous in Lopburi?
faq.a: The place most frequently cited and considered a city regular is Mat Mi Thai Phuan — a decades-old restaurant famous for its nam prik and gaeng kua hed phao. For ancient royal-style Thai cuisine, Krua Mai Hom is at the top of most lists. For a single-dish classic, Dom Khao Man Gai has been a Lopburi institution for years.

faq.q: What are the signature foods of Lopburi worth trying?
faq.a: Thai Phuan cuisine is the city's standout — try the nam prik and gaeng kua hed phao at Mat Mi Thai Phuan. Ancient Thai dishes like gaeng ranjuan and chu chi jakkraphat are at Krua Mai Hom. For noodles, there's Kuayteow Ped Phuuyai Prachum and the bold tom yam at Chalerm Thai. And don't miss the river fish at Pae Baan Rimnam.

Mostly very approachable. Noodles and chicken rice run around 40–90 THB per bowl or plate. Standard Thai dishes run around 100–160 THB per dish. Ancient Thai restaurants or riverside raft dining come to roughly 251–500 THB per person for a full meal. Cafes and fresh-milk shops start from the tens to low hundreds.

faq.q: Do I need to book a table in advance?
faq.a: Single-dish places like noodle and chicken rice shops don't need reservations — walk right in. If you're going with a large group to Krua Mai Hom, Pae Baan Rimnam, or visiting on a weekend, calling the restaurant or checking their page beforehand is a good idea, since popular places fill up on holidays.

faq.q: Are there restaurants open late into the evening?
faq.a: Yes. Nom Buri is a fresh-milk shop that opens in the evening — the right place for a late-night sit. Pae Baan Rimnam and Chalerm Thai Kuayteow Tom Yam are both good for dinner. About Coffee Garden is a garden cafe suited for the morning through afternoon. Always check the latest hours on each restaurant's page before heading out.
